record.paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Algebraic Geometry: Problems for Problem Session
record.original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let n > 1, and let Aut*_k k[n] be the group of volume-preserving polynomial k-automorphisms of affine n-space, meaning automorphisms of k[x1, ..., xn] with Jacobian determinant 1. Is every algebraic torus action on affine n-space that lies in Aut*_k k[n] linearizable? Equivalently, does Aut*_k k[n] have no maximal algebraic tori of dimension less than n - 1?

evidence.quote: The question whether Aut*_k k[n] has no maximal (with respect to inclusion) algebraic tori of dimension < n - 1 is equivalent to asking whether every 'volume preserving' algebraic torus action on A^n is linearizable.
The first nontrivial case is n = 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$ and let $n>1$. Let $\mathrm{Aut}_k k[n]$ denote the group of polynomial $k$-automorphisms of the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, identified with the group of regular automorphisms of affine $n$-space $\mathbb{A}^n_k$. Let
$$\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k[n] := \{\varphi \in \mathrm{Aut}_k k[n] : \det(\mathrm{Jac}(\varphi)) = 1\}$$
be the subgroup of volume-preserving (Jacobian determinant $1$) automorphisms. An algebraic torus action on $\mathbb{A}^n_k$ is a morphism of algebraic groups $T \to \mathrm{Aut}_k k[n]$, where $T \cong (k^*)^r$ for some $r\ge 1$; the action is called linearizable if there exist coordinates on $\mathbb{A}^n_k$ in which $T$ acts by diagonal linear transformations. Call the action volume-preserving if its image lies in $\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k[n]$.

Question: Is every volume-preserving algebraic torus action on $\mathbb{A}^n_k$ linearizable? Equivalently, is it true that $\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k[n]$ contains no maximal (with respect to inclusion) algebraic tori of dimension less than $n-1$? In particular, resolve the first nontrivial case $n=3$.
artifact.category_tag: Linearization of torus actions on affine space
artifact.status_search_result: The general linearization conjecture for torus actions on affine n-space is known in low complexity (Białynicki-Birula for codimension one; Koras-Russell and Kraft-Schwarz when fixed-point locus is positive-dimensional), but remains open in higher complexity, including the volume-preserving variant. Recent work (e.g. arXiv:2411.14645, 2024) classifies candidates for counterexamples in the codimension/complexity-two case, indicating the problem is still open, with n=3 being the first nontrivial case.

status_evidence.title: Codimension two torus actions on the affine space
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies smooth contractible affine varieties with faithful torus actions of complexity two having a unique fixed point as candidates for potential counterexamples to the linearization conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The linearization problem for torus actions on affine n-space remains open in the complexity-two case.

status_evidence.title: On linearizing algebraic torus actions
status_evidence.snippet: Białynicki-Birula's classical result establishes linearizability for codimension-one torus actions on affine space.
status_evidence.claim: Linearization is known for codimension-one tori; higher codimension cases remain unresolved.
